name: Cash Flow Posse
description: Cash Flow Posse (CFP) is a street gang that originated in Southwest Detroit, founded circa 1989 by brothers Jerry "Quick" and Bobby "Brutus" Waucaush in response to rival gang encroachment — particularly the Latin Counts and Cobras — following the collapse of the Bolo Boys. The gang became one of Southwest Detroit's most prominent criminal organizations, involved in drug trafficking and racketeering. In 1997, CFP became the first Detroit street gang prosecuted under the federal RICO Act, resulting in indictments of more than a half-dozen leaders. Incarcerated members have since linked with CFP associates to form a prison-based faction known as CountCash.
